title: Output size of the stock 4K size class: 3840x2160 to 3840x2560, in the coprocessor's movie size table (RAM) (FX2 1.01 port)
artifact: cpapp-b.bin, RAM only: these bytes are not in the file
status: addresses from emulating and reading the FX2's own code; never read or written on an FX2. The same word change (outsz2560_v1) works on the A7 IV (requests 26 to 29, F688, F698, F700)
table: movie size table 0x18f60b0 (base 0x18f6028 + 0x88; 0x4ff894 fills it; the reader 0x51fca6, case 3, loads base + 0xd0 = 0x18f60f8)

goes_with: the FX2 sensor-side design (A7 IV ogsq_v3)

sites.note: the second 3840x2160 entry (output width and height; class 4 of the FX2's table as the emulator counts it, the A7 IV's class 3) [A7 IV 0x143c7bc, A7C II 0x1a531c8]

guards.note: the entry before: 3840, 2160, memory id 0x43e [A7 IV 0x143c7b4, A7C II 0x1a531c0]
this entry's memory id, 0x2d9 [A7 IV 0x143c7c0, A7C II 0x1a531cc]

precondition: none of its own: the table is read when a movie request is set up; write it with the camera in stills, as on the A7 IV
restore: write the old word back, or cold boot (the set-up fills the table again at start-up)
checked_against: build/emu_size_table.py fx2_101 (the FX2's set-up run alone; entries equal the A7C II's)
the tbh switches of the FX2 (0x51fca6) and A7C II (0x4d436c) readers, decoded from the files: cases 0 to 5 pick the same entries
the FX2's DmmCfg.bin: id 0x2d9 = 9 x 13,271,040 bytes, as the A7 IV's
not_shown: the FX2's format code in 4K (2 on the A7 IV camera, request 25; at code 3 a 3840x2560 picture would need 14,745,600 bytes, more than the 13,271,040-byte unit)
that the reader is the only one: the scan for MOVW/MOVT of the base found one load of base + 0xd0 (0x51fcf6)
